2027-01-26.title: Tuesday after Kohne Sunday · Republic Day of India
readings: You are a letter of Christ
Give to the emperor what is the emperor's, and to God what is God's
2027-01-26.alt: Season of Denho. Republic Day of India.
2027-01-26.verse: They answered, “The emperor's.” Then he said to them, “Give therefore to the emperor the things that are the emperor's, and to God the things that are God's.”
theo: Some in Corinth wanted letters of recommendation from Paul. He answers: “You yourselves are our letter, written on our hearts, to be known and read by all; and you show that you are a letter of Christ… written not with ink but with the Spirit of the living God, not on tablets of stone but on tablets of human hearts.” The best proof of the Gospel is a changed community. And Paul is humble: “Not that we are competent of ourselves… our competence is from God.”

On Republic Day the Gospel could not be more fitting. The Pharisees and Herodians try to trap Jesus: is it lawful to pay taxes to the emperor? He asks for a coin: “Whose head is this, and whose title?” “The emperor's.” “Give therefore to the emperor the things that are the emperor's, and to God the things that are God's.” The coin bears Caesar's image; we bear God's image. Christians are loyal citizens: we pay taxes, obey just laws, vote, serve the common good and pray for those in authority. But the State is not God. Our deepest belonging is to God, and that gives us the courage to stand for justice, for the poor, and for the freedom of conscience that India's Constitution guarantees to all.
outline: Ask: whose image is on a rupee note? Whose image is on you?
“Give… to God the things that are God's.”
live: Pay what you owe honestly and obey just laws; vote with a formed conscience.
Offer God your whole self in prayer today.
2027-01-26.prayer: Lord God, you made us in your image and wrote your Spirit on our hearts. On this Republic Day bless India and its people of every faith; grant wisdom and justice to those who govern; and make us loyal citizens who give to God the things that are God's. Amen.
altar: At the Qurbono we pray for the nation and its rulers, as the Church has always done, and offer ourselves wholly to God.

quick: You are a letter of Christ written on hearts.
Give to Caesar what is Caesar's, and to God what is God's.
2027-01-26.action: Pray for India and its leaders today.
2027-01-26.question: Do I give God what belongs to God: my whole self?

family.explain: Jesus looked at a coin with the king's picture on it. He said: give the king what has his picture, and give God what has God's picture. We have God's picture in us!
family.intention: We pray for India on Republic Day.
family.ask: Ask: “How can we be good citizens and good children of God?”

illus: A schoolteacher in Kollam takes her class to hoist the flag every Republic Day and then to the parish church to pray for the country. A boy asked her why both. She said: the flag tells you whose country you serve; the cross tells you whose child you are.

pm.open: Lord, write your Spirit on our hearts and bless our nation. Amen.
share: You are a letter of Christ (2 Corinthians 3:3). What does my life say about Christ?
Our competence is from God (2 Corinthians 3:5). Do I rely on God?
Give to God the things that are God's (Matthew 22:21). What am I holding back from God?
interc: For the President, Prime Minister and all in authority.
For justice and harmony among all communities.
For our group, that we may be faithful citizens and disciples.
pm.close: Father, all authority comes from you. Bless our country and make us your faithful people. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, Paul tells the Corinthians: you show that you are a letter of Christ, written not with ink but with the Spirit of the living God, on tablets of human hearts (2 Corinthians 3:3). The best proof of the Gospel is a changed community.
And he adds: our competence is from God (2 Corinthians 3:5).

In the Gospel, on this Republic Day, Jesus says: give to the emperor the things that are the emperor's, and to God the things that are God's (Matthew 22:21). The coin bears Caesar's image; we bear God's.

So we are loyal citizens: we pay taxes, obey just laws, serve the common good and pray for our leaders. But the State is not God. Belonging to God gives us courage to stand for justice and for the freedom of conscience our Constitution guarantees to all. Amen.
kids: Children, the coin had the king's picture, but you have God's picture in you! Let us pray for India today and give our hearts to God.

intro: Theme: “Give… to God the things that are God's.”
A letter of Christ, competence from God, and faithful citizenship.

and you show that you are a letter of Christ, prepared by us, written not with ink but with the Spirit of the living God, not on tablets of stone but on tablets of human hearts.
points.apply: Let your conduct today be a letter of Christ.

q: He said to me, “This is the word of the LORD to Zerubbabel: Not by might, nor by power, but by my spirit, says the LORD of hosts.

points.apply: Begin your work with a prayer for God's help.

q: So God created humankind in his image, in the image of God he created them; male and female he created them.

points.apply: Pray for India and its leaders today.

concl: We are God's letter and God's image.
Faithful citizens, wholly belonging to God.
2027-01-26.resolve: Serve the common good in one concrete way this week.
